\section[el aprendizaje]{el aprendizaje — the learning; the apprenticeship}

\label{lesson:ES-C597-aprendizaje}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the faculty, then the Spanish for the master's degree.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el aprendizaje}
\textbf{el aprendizaje} — \textquotedblleft{}the learning; the apprenticeship\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El aprendizaje de un idioma lleva tiempo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Learning a language takes time.}
\end{quote}

A noun for the process of learning.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aprendizaje} is built on \emph{aprendiz} 'apprentice', from \emph{aprender}, inherited from Latin \emph{apprehendere} 'to seize, to grasp' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el aprendizaje}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el aprendizaje}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el aprendizaje}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the faculty, then the Spanish for the master's degree, then say \emph{el aprendizaje} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el aprendizaje mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The learning; the apprenticeship\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la enseñanza]{la enseñanza — the teaching, the education}

\label{lesson:ES-C597-ensenanza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the master's degree, then the Spanish for the learning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la enseñanza}
\textbf{la enseñanza} — \textquotedblleft{}the teaching, the education\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La enseñanza pública es gratuita.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{State education is free.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La enseñanza secundaria} — secondary education.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{enseñanza} is built on \emph{enseñar}, inherited from Medieval Latin \emph{insignare} 'to mark', from \emph{signum} 'sign' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[educar]{educar — to educate; to bring up}

\label{lesson:ES-C597-educar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the learning, then the Spanish for the teaching.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: educar}
\textbf{educar} — \textquotedblleft{}to educate; to bring up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es difícil educar a los hijos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bringing up children is difficult.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Educar a los hijos} — to bring up your children.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{educar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{educare} 'to bring up, to rear' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[evaluar]{evaluar — to assess, to evaluate}

\label{lesson:ES-C597-evaluar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the teaching, then the Spanish for to educate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: evaluar}
\textbf{evaluar} — \textquotedblleft{}to assess, to evaluate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El profesor evalúa el trabajo de todo el año.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The teacher assesses the work of the whole year.}
\end{quote}

Written accent in \emph{evalúo, evalúas, evalúa}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{evaluar} was borrowed from French \emph{évaluer}, built on \emph{value} 'worth', from Latin \emph{valere} 'to be strong, to be worth' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}

\section[la evaluación]{la evaluación — the assessment; the exam period}

\label{lesson:ES-C597-evaluacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to educate, then the Spanish for to assess.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la evaluación}
\textbf{la evaluación} — \textquotedblleft{}the assessment; the exam period\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La evaluación es en junio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The exams are in June.}
\end{quote}

In Spanish schools a school year has three \emph{evaluaciones}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{evaluación} is built on \emph{evaluar}, borrowed from French \emph{évaluer}, from Latin \emph{valere} 'to be worth' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
